title: October 5, 1864: a cyclone killed 60,000 people in Calcutta - and accidentally built India's weather-warning system.

sources.text: The Tribune - The Calcutta Cyclone of 1864: From catastrophe to India's cyclone-warning system

caption:
October 5, 1864: a cyclone killed 60,000 people in Calcutta - and accidentally built India's weather-warning system.

The Great Calcutta Cyclone of October 5, 1864, wrecked hundreds of ships, flattened warehouses across the port and killed an estimated 60,000 people - one of the deadliest cyclones ever recorded. There had been no warning system of any kind.

The scale of the disaster exposed how unprepared the region was and became one of the direct pressures that led to organized meteorological observation in India - culminating in the founding of the India Meteorological Department on January 15, 1875.

A Viksit Bharat by 2047 depends on the kind of forecasting and warning infrastructure that didn't exist in 1864 - built precisely because that absence once cost tens of thousands of lives.
